headline: Gold prices jump: 22K gold rises by 5,482 TK per bhori
summary: The price of 22-carat gold has reached 246,110 TK per bhori following the third consecutive price hike in the domestic market.
details: Gold prices in the domestic market have increased for the third consecutive time. The price of the highest quality or 22-carat gold has risen by 5,482 TK per bhori, bringing the total price to 246,110 TK.
The decision was made during a meeting of the standing committee on price determination and monitoring of the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) on Saturday morning.
The new prices became effective from 10:00 AM on August 22. According to the new list, 21-carat gold is now 235,035 TK per bhori, and 18-carat gold is 201,846 TK per bhori.
Gold of the traditional method is now priced at 164,812 TK per bhori. Silver prices have also seen an increase alongside gold.
The price of 22-carat silver is now 5,482 TK per bhori, while 21-carat silver is 5,249 TK and 18-carat silver is 4,491 TK per bhori.
Silver of the traditional method is now priced at 3,383 TK per bhori.

headline_marked: Thakurgaon-1 [[parliamentary seat declared vacant]] after Mirza Fakhrul's swearing-in
headline: Thakurgaon-1 parliamentary seat declared vacant after Mirza Fakhrul's swearing-in
summary: The Election Commission has declared the seat vacant following the appointment of the former MP as president.
details: The Election Commission has officially declared the Thakurgaon-1 parliamentary seat vacant. This follows the swearing-in of Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as president yesterday.
According to EC Secretary Abdur Rahmanel Masud, a by-election for the seat will be held within 90 days as required by law.
The process follows Article 123 of the Constitution of Bangladesh, which stipulates the timeline for filling vacant parliamentary seats.
The law also allows the Chief Election Commissioner to extend the deadline by up to another 90 days if extraordinary circumstances occur.
Possible reasons for extension include natural calamities that make it impossible to hold the election within the stipulated period.
caption:

According to EC Secretary Abdur Rahmanel Masud, a by-election for the seat will be held within 90 days as required by law.

The process follows Article 123 of the Constitution of Bangladesh, which stipulates the timeline for filling vacant parliamentary seats.

The law also allows the Chief Election Commissioner to extend the deadline by up to another 90 days if extraordinary circumstances occur.

Possible reasons for extension include natural calamities that make it impossible to hold the election within the stipulated period.
